title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Approving the Fujian High People's Court to Carry Out the Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases
keywords_en: administrative litigation; High People's Court conducting administrative cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Reply on Approving the Fujian High People's Court to Carry Out the Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases

Fa [2019] No. 157

Fujian High People's Court:

Your Request for Instructions on Designating Fuzhou Railway Transport Court to Accept Some Administrative, Ecological and Environmental, and Enforcement Cases (Min Gao Fa [2019] No. 137) has been received. Upon study, in accordance with the provisions of Article 18, Paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the spirit of the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on People's Courts' Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases across Administrative Regions (Fa Fa [2015] No. 8), we approve in principle your request.

Please, under the unified leadership and coordination of the local Party committee, advance the reform in line with the spirit of the central institutional reform and the requirements of institutional reform in your region. When refining and implementing the reform plan, the administrative adjudication functions of the basic people's courts in various localities should be retained to maintain the integrity of the litigation system and to serve the local work of law-based administration. The intermediate people's courts may select one or two basic people's courts with a large number of cases, strong adjudication capabilities, a good judicial environment, and convenient transportation as central courts to exercise centralized jurisdiction. The plaintiff's right to choose shall be fully respected; the plaintiff may choose either the court where the defendant is located or the central court. Local courts and centralized jurisdiction courts shall strengthen communication and coordination, coordinate the separation of adjudication and mediation and the combination of adjudication and mediation, and jointly do a good job in coordinating and resolving administrative disputes. If railway courts are used to centrally accept some administrative cases, specific issues such as the transfer of key administrative adjudication personnel must be properly handled first to avoid a decline in the quality of administrative adjudication, and the future reform direction of railway courts and the centralized jurisdiction over other cases should also be considered simultaneously. A mechanism for unifying adjudication standards shall be established to prevent inconsistency in adjudication standards for similar cases due to different courts having jurisdiction. Before the Plan is implemented, it shall be announced publicly. Your court shall strengthen research and guidance, and promptly report new situations and problems arising during implementation to the Supreme People's Court.
